title: Hawthorne Bindery's Last Chapter
setting: A sun-faded cobblestone alley in coastal Massachusetts, where the red brick Portside Small Library juts into a cramped, oak-lined bookbindery run by the Hawthorne family for 73 years. The bindery’s back shelves are stacked with leather-bound classics and half-finished custom journals, and the air smells like waxed thread and old paper; the library’s director has just notified the family the town council will cut their shared rental space in three months to make way for a free public wifi hub.

characters.name: Elias Hawthorne
characters.tendencies: He has run the Hawthorne Bindery for 45 years, refusing to adopt modern binding equipment because he believes hand-tooled craft is the only way to honor the vintage books the library houses.

characters.name: Lila Hawthorne
characters.tendencies: She is Elias’ 26-year-old granddaughter and the bindery’s only apprentice, and she wants to launch a hybrid model of hand binding and digital design templates to keep the business operational after their rental space is lost.

characters.name: Marisol "Marcy" Hale
characters.tendencies: She has served as Portside Small Library’s director for 12 years, and she is lobbying the town council to reallocate part of the wifi hub budget to carve out a dedicated bindery space in the library’s basement.

characters.name: Tom Mendez
characters.tendencies: He is a 17-year-old high school poet and book club president who orders custom journals from the Hawthorne Bindery for his club’s annual chapbook, and he organized a 220-signature petition to keep the bindery open for local creators.
